questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal when turning from this lane.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is about to end. If you are turning in that direction, prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before you turn.

questions.question: When merging onto an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
Cross two lanes at the same time.
Always stop before entering the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe gap and merge into traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, find a gap that is large enough for your vehicle to safely enter the traffic flow. Do not stop on the entrance ramp unless there are no safe gaps to merge into.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:

options.text: Making sudden, unsafe lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.
Driving slowly.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers while you drive. If you see an aggressive driver making sudden or unsafe lane changes, do not challenge them. The safest thing to do is to move away from them.

questions.question: Why should you give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: They do not react as quickly as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Be extra careful near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Watch for children on bikes on the sidewalk—they may move into the road without warning.

questions.question: What does this pennant-shaped sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Right turn permitted on red.
Yield right-of-way.

questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks where passing is not allowed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Highway entrance ramp.
Road widens.
Right lane ends.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the right lane is ending. Be ready for traffic to merge from the right.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal quickly several times.
Slow down slowly and do not use the brakes.
Press the brake pedal as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down slowly and do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Take your foot off the gas pedal. Do not brake hard. Let the car slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if you need to. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at railroad crossings (school buses, trucks carrying hazardous materials, etc.).
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Be very careful at all railroad crossings. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Know which vehicles must stop at all railroad crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Can you leave the engine running when all passengers have left a vehicle?

options.text: No, never.
Yes, if you will only be gone a couple minutes.
Yes, if you will be gone for less than an hour.

questions.explanation: You must turn off the engine and remove the key from the ignition when you leave a vehicle. Always lock your vehicle when you leave it, even if you will only be away for a short time.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Look straight ahead at all times.
Only look at the center of the road.
Watch the sides, front, and back of their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the sides, front, and back of their car.
questions.explanation: You need to watch the sides, front, and back of your car. Good drivers know what is happening all around their vehicle.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that makes you swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind away from driving. It is the leading cause of traffic crashes. Any distraction causes drivers to miss important things they need to see and hear to avoid a crash.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Make you a better driver.
Make you feel better.
Hurt your judgment.

questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, being sleepy slows your reaction time, reduces your awareness, and hurts your judgment.

questions.question: A driver ahead stops at a crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Pass carefully at 10 mph or slower.
Stop and go only after all pedestrians have crossed.
Change lanes, look, and pass the stopped car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and go only after all pedestrians have crossed.
questions.explanation: Do not pass a car stopped at a crosswalk. There may be pedestrians you cannot see. Stop and go only after all pedestrians have crossed.

questions.question: As blood alcohol level (BAC) goes up, you become:

options.text: More drunk.
More sober.
More coordinated.

questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: When approaching a curve, you should slow down:

options.text: Only if you want to.
Before you enter the curve.
Halfway through the curve.

questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve so you will not need to brake hard in the curve. Braking in a curve can cause you to skid and lose control.

questions.question: Adjust your mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need them.
Before you get in the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you drive. Before moving, also adjust your seat, fasten your seat belt, and secure items. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: When a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing:

options.text: You must always let them cross first.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only must let them cross at intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always let them cross first.
questions.explanation: Blind people use a white cane or guide dog. You must always let these pedestrians cross first.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming cars are going. They may seem slower than they really are. Always make sure you can safely change lanes before passing. If you are not sure, wait until the oncoming car passes and you have plenty of space.

questions.question: A red curb means:

options.text: Loading zone.
You can pick up or drop off passengers.
No parking, standing, or stopping.

questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
How fast you drive does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly is dangerous. Other drivers may get frustrated and make unsafe moves to pass you. The safest approach is to drive with traffic flow, within the speed limit.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Fight the feeling.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.explanation: Stop at a rest stop or service area to rest, nap, stretch, or change drivers. Do not rely on caffeine pills or energy drinks. They are not a real solution and may make your driving more dangerous.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding and driving too fast for current conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding and driving too fast for current conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding above the limit and driving too fast for conditions cause many crashes. Always drive within the speed limit and adjust your speed for road and weather conditions.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Stop sign ahead.
Divided highway.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow. In this case, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?

options.text: Drink strong coffee.
Wait.
Take a cold shower.

questions.explanation: Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, or showers cannot speed this up.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive while taking medication that affects your driving?

options.text: Never.
Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while impaired by any substance. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: Why do work zones use barriers, drums, cones, and signs?

options.text: To make drivers frustrated.
To inconvenience drivers.
To keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. These warn you and direct traffic safely.

questions.question: When leaving a parallel parking space, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Look over your shoulder.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: If parked on the right side, turn on your left signal and look over your left shoulder. If parked on the left side of a one-way street, turn on your right signal and look over your right shoulder before entering traffic.

questions.question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:

options.text: At all times.
Only during school hours.
Unless you do not see any children present.

questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools. Watch for them and follow their instructions.

questions.question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one vehicle moves faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving too fast or too slow compared to traffic increases the risk of a crash. A slow vehicle can cause rear-end collisions or make other drivers swerve.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, the effects of alcohol will be reduced only by:

options.text: Taking a cold shower.
Waiting several hours.
Drinking several cups of coffee.

questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Cold showers, coffee, or exercise will not help. Your body needs about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: If a traffic signal light is green and a police officer signals for you to stop, you should:

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic signal.
Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's instructions, even if they contradict a traffic signal or sign.

questions.question: If your vehicle has mechanical trouble while on a public road and you need to stop, you should:

options.text: Stop where you are and turn on your hazard lights.
Stop where you are and hold down your horn.
Pull off the right side of the road and turn on your hazard lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and turn on your hazard lights.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, pull to the right side of the road if you can. Turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road ahead curves left then right.
The road ahead curves right then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right then left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the road will curve right, then curve left. Slow down and be ready to turn.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: If you are driving and you see animals standing near the roadway:

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly run into traffic. There may also be more animals nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip the road better than when you are driving on pavement.
Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads have less traction than pavement. Slow down because it takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: When you are driving on the interstate and see that another vehicle will be entering your lane from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Speed up to pass them.
Change lanes to allow them room to safely merge.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to allow them room to safely merge.
questions.explanation: Help vehicles merge safely onto the interstate. Change lanes when you can to give them room to enter smoothly.
